signals.name: NVIDIA Corporation
signals.label: Congress tech-committee buying meets a huge retail mention spike
signals.detail: Rep. John McGuire (R-VA-5, House Armed Services Cyber/Innovative Technologies subcommittee) disclosed on 2026-09-02 a fresh $1,001-$15,000 NVDA buy dated 2026-08-18 in his Merrill Lynch SEP IRA -- his third NVDA buy of 2026, with local reporting noting a pattern of buying shortly before NVIDIA AI-deal announcements. Separately, r/wallstreetbets mention volume for NVDA spiked sharply week-over-week per ApeWisdom/AltIndex trackers as of 2026-09-28, amid Monday's broad market selloff (S&P500 -0.77%, VIX +8.07% to 16.07).
signals.takeaway: Repeated small-dollar congressional buying by a member with Armed Services cyber-tech visibility lines up with a large retail chatter spike right as the broader market absorbed a volatility shock -- watch whether retail buys the dip.

signals.name: Micron Technology, Inc.
signals.label: Retail mania vs. Michael Burry's fresh short, days before earnings
signals.detail: On 2026-09-22 Michael Burry posted on his Cassandra Unchained Substack that he added 'in some size' to shorts in Micron (plus Nebius, Palantir, SOXX), arguing MU is more technically extended than at any point since 1984 and that DRAM oversupply could return as capacity shifts back from HBM -- landing days before Micron's Sept 30 fiscal Q4 earnings. Congress is split: several members bought MU in June-July while Rep. Gil Cisneros sold roughly $1,001-$15,000 across two May trades. Retail is loud: MU mentions on r/wallstreetbets jumped sharply on 2026-09-28, ranking among the most-discussed tickers.
signals.takeaway: A textbook divergence -- a prominent short-seller presses a bearish bet into earnings while retail chatter peaks and Congress itself is split; Sept 30 earnings is the near-term resolution.

signals.name: Palantir Technologies Inc.
signals.label: Ethics scrutiny + Burry short + ARK exit, but retail has gone quiet
signals.detail: Rep. Gil Cisneros (D-CA-31, House Armed Services) was flagged in a September 2026 report for filing 50+ trades late, including Palantir purchases -- notable given PLTR's government/defense contract exposure overlapping his committee seat. The same week, Burry disclosed (2026-09-22 Substack post) adding to his Palantir short, and Cathie Wood's ARK funds had already sold PLTR (with AMD) around 2026-09-08 to fund new Robinhood and Cerebras buys. Despite this, PLTR does not crack the top of the most-mentioned tickers on r/wallstreetbets as of 2026-09-28.
signals.takeaway: Three separate oversight/'smart money' signals turned cautious-to-bearish on Palantir in the same two-week window, while its once-signature retail buzz has notably cooled.

signals.name: Microsoft Corporation
signals.label: Ex-Microsoft-exec congressman's seven-figure buy, retail warms too
signals.detail: Rep. Josh Gottheimer (D-NJ-5) -- a former Microsoft executive who sits on House Financial Services and House Intelligence -- disclosed on 2026-09-14 a $753,005-$1,545,000 MSFT common-stock purchase dated 2026-08-14, alongside an options 'roll' (Oct 2026 calls bought, Dec 2026 calls sold same day) reported to echo a March 2026 MSFT-calls trade. Retail interest rose more modestly: MSFT mentions on r/wallstreetbets up week-over-week as of 2026-09-28.
signals.takeaway: A congressman with direct Microsoft experience keeps making large, well-timed MSFT trades -- worth tracking regardless of retail's calmer but positive interest.

signals.name: Broadcom Inc.
signals.label: Congress keeps buying the chip name macro funds are split on
signals.detail: Q2 2026 13F filings (disclosed mid-August) showed a split: David Tepper's Appaloosa opened a new AVGO stake (one of the few funds adding), while Dan Loeb's Third Point and Stanley Druckenmiller's Duquesne fully exited AVGO, rotating proceeds into TSM. Congress stayed net-bullish -- Rep. Rick Allen added a fresh $1,001-$15,000 buy dated 2026-08-12 (disclosed 2026-09-22).
signals.takeaway: Congress and one star macro fund (Tepper) are buying while two other marquee investors (Loeb, Druckenmiller) bailed entirely -- a genuine split on AVGO's AI-capex exposure.

signals.name: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited
signals.label: Where Tepper, Loeb, Druckenmiller -- and Congress -- are rotating into
signals.detail: The same Q2 2026 13F wave that showed funds fleeing Broadcom showed them piling into TSM: Appaloosa, Third Point (while exiting AVGO/NVDA outright) and Duquesne all added TSM shares, while TSM itself raised FY26 revenue guidance to 'slightly above 40%' growth. Congress piled in too: Rep. Rick Allen bought TSM on 2026-08-19 (disclosed 2026-09-22/23) the same week he bought AVGO.
signals.takeaway: TSM is the rare name where congressional buying and three top macro/hedge funds line up bullish -- a genuine multi-source consensus pick, in contrast to the AVGO split.

signals.name: Tesla, Inc.
signals.label: Congress trims, a top Musk backer cashes out, but retail chatter reignites
signals.detail: Rep. Gil Cisneros disclosed selling $1,001-$15,000 of TSLA (traded 2026-08-18, disclosed 2026-09-10/12) in the same late-filed batch as his PLTR/MSFT trades. Separately, Valor Equity Partners -- a top institutional backer of SpaceX and Tesla run by Musk ally Antonio Gracias -- distributed roughly $8.5B of SpaceX stock to its own fund investors in mid-September. Countering that caution, Ron Baron of Baron Capital, one of Tesla's largest long-term holders, went on CNBC in September reaffirming his bullish Musk thesis. TSLA mentions on r/wallstreetbets rose sharply on 2026-09-28.
signals.takeaway: A congressional seller and a major insider distribution event sit next to renewed retail buzz and a top holder's on-air reaffirmation -- genuinely mixed signals on Tesla right now.
